differences: The recording file names carry a ground or board tag that disagrees with the authors' postural stability variable on 680 of 2640 rows, all of them in participant 2's rounds (rounds 2 and 4); this tag is not used. The condition here is the authors' postural_stability variable, which is also the condition column of their f0 and pause-duration tables. The gyroscope backs it: the board moves (angular velocity RMS about 13 deg/s) on exactly the rows labelled board and is at rest (about 0) on the ground rows of participant 1, whereas the file name tags of participant 2's rounds would put board trials on rows where the board did not move. In the authors' analysis variable, therefore, participant 2 of every pair stands on the ground in round 2 and on the board in round 4, and only participant 1's order is counterbalanced across pairs (the paper says the order was counterbalanced over pairs without saying for which partner).

The exclusion file's own gyro_tilt_sd_x column (values near 140 to 180) looks like the SD of an angle that wraps at 180 degrees (the paper uses the unwrapped angle) and is not used; the board_trial_metrics table (tilt SD 0.7 to 14.6 degrees), whose clue-giver means reproduce the paper's manipulation check, is used for the board metrics. The exclusion file also holds gyro values on ground trials (board at rest, near zero); they are not copied.

The paper's text gives 2305 trials with a mean amplitude envelope; the shared table has 2303 valid trials with one, the same as for speech rate (2303), while the f0 count (2295) and all other counts match, so the 2305 looks like an error in the text. The stability_condition column of the authors' pause_duration table copies the ground or board tag of the recording file name, so it disagrees with the analysis variable on 578 of its 2183 rows (their R script takes the condition from the exclusion file); it is not used.

The paper's condition means are estimated marginal means of mixed models (negative binomial for the counts); the values here are averages of the participants' own condition means over the valid trials, so they can differ slightly (the checks use a tolerance).
